extracted.intended_audience: lawmakers, patent practitioners, patent applicants, and stakeholders reviewing H.R. 1908 (Patent Reform Act of 2007)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and interpret statutory requirements and procedural rules in H.R. 1908 (Patent Reform Act of 2007) affecting patentability, post‑grant and derivation procedures, inventor declarations, and related definitions and effective‑date conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions added to Section 100
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds definitions: (f) 'inventor' means the individual or, if a joint invention, the individuals collectively who invented or discovered the subject matter of an invention; (g) 'joint inventor' and 'coinventor' mean any one of the individuals who invented or discovered the subject matter of a joint invention; (h) 'effective filing date of a claimed invention' is the filing date of the patent or application containing the claim or, if entitled to priority/benefit under specified sections, the filing date of the earliest such application in which the claimed invention is disclosed as provided by section 112(a); (i) 'claimed invention' means the subject matter defined by a claim in a patent or application; (j) 'joint invention' means an invention resulting from collaboration of two or more persons working toward the same end and producing an invention by their collective efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory definitions govern how later provisions (novelty, priority, derivation, etc.) are applied; they clarify who counts as an inventor/joint inventor and how 'effective filing date' is computed (including priority/continuation chains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for patentability; novelty (Section 102(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: "(a) Novelty; Prior Art.—A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained if— (1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, in public use, or on sale— (A) more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; or (B) one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention, other than through disclosures made by the inventor or a joint inventor or by others who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor; or (2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the statutory novelty bars and a one‑year grace window tied to the effective filing date; also addresses prior patents or published applications that name a different inventor and were effectively filed earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior inventor disclosure exception (Section 102(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that would otherwise qualify as prior art under subsection (a)(1)(B) shall not be prior art to a claimed invention under that subparagraph if the subject matter had, before such disclosure, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or others who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects an inventor's prior public disclosures (or disclosures by those who derived from the inventor) from counting as prior art against the inventor's later filing, within the statutory grace framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation, prior disclosure, and common assignment exceptions (Section 102(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that would otherwise qualify as prior art only under subsection (a)(2) shall not be prior art to a claimed invention if— (A) the subject matter was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor; (B) the subject matter had been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or others who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor before the earlier effective filing date; or (C) the subject matter and the claimed invention, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are exceptions to prior‑art effect where derivation, prior inventor disclosure, or common ownership/assignment means the earlier filing should not bar patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement exception (Section 102(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter and a claimed invention shall be deemed to have been owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment for purposes of paragraph (2) if— (i) the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the effective filing date; (ii) the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (iii) the application for patent for the claimed invention discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement. 'Joint research agreement' means a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement entered into by two or more persons or entities for performance of experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conditions under which collaborative research negates certain prior‑art effects by treating the earlier subject matter and the claimed invention as commonly owned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents and published applications effectively filed (Section 102(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent or application for patent is effectively filed with respect to any subject matter described in the patent or application— (A) as of the filing date of the patent or application; or (B) if entitled to claim priority/benefit under specified sections, as of the filing date of the earliest such application that describes the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when a patent or application counts as 'effectively filed' for prior art comparisons (important for determining novelty and priority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for patentability; nonobvious subject matter (Section 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained though the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restates the statutory non‑obviousness test and clarifies that the method of making the invention does not defeat patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of requirements for inventions made abroad (Section 104 repeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 104 (and its table entry) are repealed, removing statutory requirements concerning where inventions were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates any prior statutory bar tied to inventions made abroad (conforming U.S. practice to not require U.S. origin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceeding initiation requirements (Section 135(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request initiation of a derivation proceeding by filing a request that sets forth with particularity the basis for finding that another applicant derived the claimed invention and, without authorization, filed an application claiming such invention. Any such request— (i) may only be made within 12 months after the earlier of (I) the date on which a patent is issued containing a claim that is the same or substantially the same as the claimed invention; or (II) the date of first publication of an application containing such a claim; and (ii) must be made under oath, and must be supported by substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes strict timing (12‑month) and evidentiary/oath requirements for initiating derivation proceedings to resolve disputes over who has the right to a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to institute derivation proceeding (Section 135(a)(1)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Director determines that patents or applications naming different individuals as the inventor interfere with one another because of a dispute over the right to patent on the basis of a request, the Director shall institute a derivation proceeding for the purpose of determining which applicant is entitled to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places responsibility on the Director to institute derivation proceedings when the statutory conditions are met; initiation follows the particularity/timing/evidence requirements described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB determination and effect of final decision in derivation proceedings (Section 135(a)(2) & (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding under this subsection, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall determine the question of the right to patent; in appropriate circumstances may correct the naming of the inventor; and shall issue a final decision on the right to patent. The final decision of the Board, if adverse to the claim of an applicant, shall constitute the final refusal by the PTO on the claims involved. The Director may issue a patent to an applicant who is determined by the Board to have the right to a patent. The final decision of the Board, if adverse to a patentee, shall, if no appeal or other review has been or can be taken, constitute cancellation of the claims involved, and notice of such cancellation shall be endorsed on copies of the patent distributed after such cancellation by the PTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the PTAB's authority to resolve derivation disputes, correct inventorship, issue final decisions that affect issuance and cancellation of claims, and the administrative effects of adverse determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceeding timing; PTAB deferral (Section 135(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board may defer action on a request to initiate a derivation proceeding for up to three months after the date on which the Director issues a patent to the applicant that filed the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows a short administrative deferral to accommodate recently issued earlier patents before proceeding with derivation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration; naming inventors and execution (Section 115(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent must include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor of any claimed invention. Except as otherwise provided, each individual who is the inventor or a joint inventor of a claimed invention in an application for patent shall execute an oath or declaration in connection with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates inventor naming and personal statements as part of the application; foundational requirement for filing and later allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statements in the inventor's oath or declaration (Section 115(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must contain statements that— (1) the application was made or was authorized to be made by the individual; and (2) the individual believes himself or herself to be the original inventor or an original joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the minimal attestations inventors must make under oath or declaration when filing or being named in an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may specify additional information; substitute statement permitted (Section 115(c) & (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may specify additional information to be included in an oath or declaration. In lieu of executing an oath or declaration, the applicant may provide a substitute statement if the individual is unable to file because (A) deceased; (B) under legal incapacity; (C) cannot be found or reached after diligent effort; or (D) is under an obligation to assign the invention and has refused to make the oath or declaration. A substitute statement must identify the individual, set forth the circumstances representing the permitted basis for filing the substitute statement, and contain any additional information required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides alternative compliance paths when an inventor cannot execute an oath/declaration and gives the Director regulatory discretion to require further particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making required statements in assignment of record; notice of allowance timing (Section 115(e)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual under an obligation of assignment may include the required statements in the assignment executed by the individual, in lieu of filing such statements separately. A notice of allowance may be provided to an applicant only if the applicant has filed each required oath or declaration or has filed a substitute statement or recorded an assignment meeting the requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits required inventorship statements to be satisfied by properly executed assignments and conditions allowance on having the required statements on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental and corrected statements; savings clause (Section 115(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a statement required may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time; if a change in naming requires additional statements, such must be filed per Director regulations. If an individual has executed an oath or declaration or an acceptable assignment, the Director may not thereafter require that individual to make additional equivalent statements in connection with the application or any patent issuing thereon. No patent shall be invalid or unenforceable based upon failure to comply with a requirement under this section if the failure is remedied as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows correction and supplementation of inventor statements and protects patents from invalidation for remediable defects in inventor statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of penalties in declarations (Section 115(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed under this section must contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement is punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both, under section 1001 of title 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires an explicit penalty acknowledgment to deter and penalize willful falsity in inventor statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by other than inventor (Section 118)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention may make an application for patent. A person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest may make an application on behalf of and as agent for the inventor on proof of pertinent facts and a showing that such action is appropriate to preserve the rights of the parties. If the Director grants a patent on such an application, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest and upon such notice to the inventor as the Director considers sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits assignees or agents with proprietary interest to file; the patent is issued to the real party in interest with appropriate notice to the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date conditions for these amendments (Section 3(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments take effect 90 days after the President transmits to Congress a finding that major patenting authorities have adopted a grace period having substantially the same effect as contained in these amendments, and shall apply to all applications filed on or after that effective date. 'Major patenting authorities' means at least Europe and Japan. 'Grace period' means the 1-year period ending on the effective filing date during which disclosures by the inventor/joint inventor or those who obtained the subject matter from them do not qualify as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions the effective date on international harmonization of a similar grace period and specifies retrospective scope (applications filed on/after effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review requirement (Section 3(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than the end of the 7‑year period beginning on the effective date, and every 7‑year period thereafter, the Director shall conduct a study on the effectiveness and efficiency of the amendments made by this section and submit to the Judiciary Committees a report on the results, including any recommendations on amendments to the law and the first‑to‑file system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates recurring evaluation of the statute's implementation and effectiveness with reporting to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of references to 'interferences' and replacement with 'derivation proceedings' and 'Patent Trial and Appeal Board' (Section 3(j) and related conforming amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strikes references to the 'Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences' and inserts 'Patent Trial and Appeal Board' throughout; replaces references to 'interference' with 'derivation proceeding' and updates section headings (e.g., 'Sec. 134. Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board', 'Sec. 135. Derivation proceedings', etc.). Subsection 1295(a)(4)(A) of title 28 is amended to make appeals to the PTAB for specified proceedings and to require waiver of rights to proceed under sections 145 or 146 in certain appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernizes nomenclature and aligns appeals and proceedings with the new PTAB/derivation framework; affects forum and appellate routes for applicants and parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of statutory invention registration (Section 157 repeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 157 (statutory invention registration) and its table entry are repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes the statutory option of statutory invention registration from the code (administrative change to available mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier filing date wording for inventor/joint inventor (Section 3(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 120 is amended by striking 'which is filed by an inventor or inventors named' and inserting 'which names an inventor or joint inventor'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical amendment clarifying that the controlling factor is naming an inventor or joint inventor for earlier filing date purposes.
